findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed one adult and one juvenile roach in the kitchen near the fryers and wok grill. Both pests were under or within equipment and not on food-contact surfaces. Orkin treated for pests yesterday, September 10, 2026. Orkin will continue to treat weekly for the next five weeks. Continue cleaning efforts in the kitchen to limit the pest’s food availability. Ensure all food containers are tightly sealed when not in use. Remove all unnecessary cardboard from the facility, as it acts as a food source and area of harborage. Ensure staff are NEVER using their own chemical to treat for pests. Only licensed, professional pest control operators are spraying chemical in the facility. A 30-day follow-up will be conducted on October 9, 2026 to ensure pest presence continues to improve in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a cardboard box without a lid to be used for food storage of fried rice noodles. The box was also observed contaminated by multiple cockroaches. The staff were informed that cardboard boxes are not a smooth, easily cleanable surface for food storage. The box was discarded during the inspection. Ensure all food items are stored in plastic or metal containers with tight-fitting lids.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors EJ and AD observed multiple live cockroaches present under the wok grill near the service line in the kitchen. All roaches observed were fast moving. Pests were observed on top of and underneath the wok grill, on the spice cart containing open spice and sauce containers, annd within a cardboard box containing fried rice noodles. Inspectors strongly recommend placing glue traps around the facility for pest monitoring. Staff should NEVER be spraying their own chemical in the kitchen for pest control. The only sprays used in the facility should be administered by authorized pest control professionals only. Due to the presence of pests on food-contact surfaces, the facility will voluntarily close today to conduct a deep cleaning. The facility can open again tomorrow, September 10th pending pest control treatment and authorization from the public health inspector.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a metal scrubber stored in the basin of the hand sink next to the ice machine. The person in charge (PIC) was informed and the scrubber was removed. Ensure staff are using the triple sink or utility sink to scrub dishes and never the hand sinks. This violation was corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the egg rolls to be stored in direct contact with a washing cloth. This cloth was heavily saturated with water. The PIC stated that the egg rolls release water as they thaw and become soggy in the metal container. Inspector recommends using a straining insert to keep the egg rolls dry and prevent cross-contamination. Ensure egg rolls are stored properly to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.13 Linens and Napkins, Use Limitation. LINENS, such as cloth napkins, may not be used in contact with FOOD unless they are used to line a container for the service of FOODS and the LINENS and napkins are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new CONSUMER.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a knife to be stored in the crevice between the prep cooler and stainless steel countertop. The PIC was informed that this crevice is not easily cleanable. Therefore, the knife cannot be stored here. The inspector recommends purchasing a magnetic knife block to attach to the shelf of the prep cooler for safe storage. The knife was moved to the dish area during today’s visit. This violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wastewater leak coming from the hand sink to the left of the grill. The leak is coming from the connection between the PVC plumbing and the metal sink basin. Wastewater leaks pose a cross-contamination hazard, especially located so close to the cook line. A follow-up will be conducted on Monday, June 22, 2026 to ensure the leak has been repaired.

Repeat Violation

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed breaded chicken cooling on the counter in the kitchen. The PIC informed inspectors that the chicken had been prepared “this morning.” The chicken measured 90F with the infrared thermometer. The inspector discussed proper cooling with the PIC and the chicken was placed in the walk-in cooler. Ensure items are kept on the counter to cool ONLY until they reach 135F. At that time, items need to be transferred to a cooler to complete cooling within the required time-frame.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the facility’s cooling units. Ambient thermometers help the facility monitor cold holding temperatures, to ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are at the correct temperature (41F and below) to mitigate the growth of pathogens. Ensure the facility obtains ambient thermometers in cooling units (with freezers being an exception) to monitor cold holding temperatures by the next routine inspection. Place ambient thermometers in the warmest part of the cooling unit (towards the front).

[C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Raw shrimp, cooked chicken wings, and andouille sausage stored in the prep cooler were observed to be above the maximum cold holding temperature (41F). PIC stated that the raw shrimp had been placed in the cooler that morning, and the chicken wings and sausage were recently added to the prep cooler. The shrimp, since it had been out of temp for an unknown time, was voluntarily discarded. The chicken wings and sausage were placed in the walk-in cooler for reach an appropriate temperature. Below are the probed temperatures measured from the items:
1. Raw shrimp : 48F
2. Chicken wings : 48F
3. Andouille Sausage : 51F

Ensure staff are measuring the temperature of items in the cooler to ensure compliance. Since the items were either discarded or placed in the walk-in, the violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed fish to be thawing in still water at ambient temperature. The temperature of the fish in water was 63F (probe). Since the fish was improperly thawed, the items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are either thawing in the cooler or under running water.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed thawed fish to be in its original reduced oxygen packaging. The packaging indicated that the fish needed to be removed from packaging before thawing. Thawing the fish in its reduced oxygen packaging can promote the proliferation of the bacteria responsible for botulism. Ensure staff are removing the fish from its packaging prior to thawing. The fish was voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that facility has no food handler’s certificates available on site. All employees who handle food need to have a food handler’s certificate within 30 days of employment. Ensure employees have food handler’s certification available for view prior to next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Ensure no CFPM onsite to have valid allergen certification CFPM confirmed she has not taken the course. Ensure there is a CFPM onsite with allergen certification at all times. 


410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizing solution in use in kitchen to test at 50 ppm Cl-. Sanitizing solution was remade during inspection and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed containers of crawfish, clams, green mussels and black mussels to temp at 61F. All items found out of temperature were discarded during inspection. Per PIC, items were placed into prep cooler immediately after boiling. I advised PIC to discontinue this process. Prep cooler is holding all other foods at proper temperatures. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed no CFPM to be on duty while food is being prepared and served. Provide a CFPM on duty at all times of food preparation and service. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed container of cooked chicken and cooked rice noodles in prep cooler to not have a date mark. Per PIC, items were prepared on 3/21/24. Items were marked with proper date during inspection.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed two packages of sausage to be thawing at room temperature on 3 compartment sink. Sausage was placed under running water to thaw during inspection.

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed facility to be unable to provided food handler certification for food employees. Provide food handler certifications for all food employees that do not possess a certified food protection manager certification. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Observed facility to have several foundation and foundation priority items during inspection. Correct foundation and foundation priority items identified during inspection. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed facility to not have signed employee reporting agreements for food employees. Provide signed reporting agreements for all food employees.

2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.comment:
Observed 2 steel wool pads in basin of hand washing sink at bar. Steel wool pads were removed during inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed baffle of ice machine in kitchen to be soiled with pink debris. Clean and sanitize baffle of ice machine. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed pieces of cardboard placed over vents above grill and fryers in kitchen. Cardboard was removed during inspection.

P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. findings.comment:
Observed facility to not have test strips for quaternary ammonia sanitizer. Facility only has chlorine test strips. Provide quaternary ammonia test strips. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.
